brief: The canvas displays a dynamically winding molecular structure, representing the DNA double helix. The backbone is constructed from spheres, each labeled with a single letter: A, T, C, or G. These spheres connect into two winding strands that spiral around a central axis. The core feature is the formation of explicit hydrogen bonds. At various points along the helix, pairs of complementary base spheres (such as A and T, or C and G) will dynamically approach one another, temporary bonds will visibly snap into place between them, and this bonding process will continuously undulate and stabilize, creating a complex, moving molecular diagram.

statement: This sketch renders a dynamically animated DNA double helix using p5.js in WEBGL mode. The structure consists of two intertwined strands made from spheres representing nucleotide bases (A, T, C, G), which spiral around a central axis with subtle undulations. Hydrogen bonds form between complementary base pairs (A-T and C-G) at various points along the helix, creating temporary connections that pulse and stabilize over time. The visualization uses batching techniques to stay within performance constraints while maintaining visual complexity, showing both the molecular structure and the dynamic bonding process in real-time.
